description: This one-of-a-kind property, built in 1432. is among the oldest standing houses in Paris, It has been faithfully restored and updated by a well-known New York designer, and is located on a quiet "old town" corner in Paris' Marais district.The spaceMaison 1400 is a landmark 15th Century townhouse that has been renovated to the highest standards and decorated with impeccable style. One of the oldest houses in Paris (circa 1432), it is a robust structure of thick stone walls, many fireplaces, ancient wood-beamed ceilings and myriad floors of terra cotta tile, oak plank and cut limestone.It is located in the heart of the Old Marais, or 4th arrondisement, near Hôtel de Ville and Pompidou Center. The neighborhood is teeming with restaurants, shops, museums and is considered the liveliest quarter in town, yet our street is very quiet. Nearby Rue Rambuteau is the local market street with a variety food purveyors of all kinds, including award-winning bakeries.. The house features several living areas, four bedrooms, four and a half baths, one gourmet kitchen and three kitchenettes. It functions a vertical townhouse that can sleep up to eight persons in four private, self-contained suites. It is decorated with antique, period-style and contemporary furnishings with fine art to complement the faithfully restored medieval architecture. It showcases the designer's signature style of understated luxury, harmony and comfort. The suites are spread out over 3 stories, organized at half-levels around a 'landmark' circular stairwell with original carved stand-post & tomette tiles.MAîTRE SUITE: (a 2-level suite) accommodating 1-2 persons:High ceilings, massive oak beams, limestone tiles and wide-plank flooring are hallmarks of the largest apartment.
